metadata.title: A Primer on Resurgent Transseries and Their Asymptotics

extraction_notes.note: The paper declares theorem environments but never uses them; almost all content is in 586 numbered equation environments linked by running-text derivations. Each numbered equation is an equation node, and uses edges between consecutive equations of a derivation were added by judgment from phrases such as 'it follows', 'leading to', 'one obtains'.
Equation (stokespheno) was retyped equation -> claim because a later prose proof (section 5, 'we are still short of a proof for such statement') explicitly proves it.
Numbered equations the text names as results (Cauchy's theorem, the Picard--Lefschetz formula, the Ecalle connection formulae) were retyped as external theorems rather than left as equations.

Seven numbered equations that restate earlier ones verbatim or near-verbatim ('recall', 'we reproduce in here') got no node: restatements of stokesauto, the Stokes automorphism exponential, the non-resonance condition, the vanishing Stokes-coefficient conditions, the quartic potential, and the one-parameter transseries and its sectors.

Boxed 'statistical mechanical' rules (Ovalbox) for Stokes discontinuities and large-order relations were taken as one node each, spanning the box and the equation that spells it out; discontinuity boxes are definitions (the paper calls them its definition) and large-order boxes are semi-formal claims.

Section 3 says 'let us justify this construction' and then introduces thimbles, gradient flows and vanishing cycles. These were kept as Level-1 definitions rather than proof steps; only the closing intersection-pairing paragraph was taken as the proof of the thimble decomposition.
Two exercises are stated inside footnotes. Their spans start inside the footnote, which the finishing step flags as a mid-sentence start (warning only).

Content carried only by figures (alien-chain and alien-lattice diagrams in figure floats, Pade-pole and Richardson-transform plots), the KAM-theory digression, the acknowledgements and the bibliography were not extracted as nodes.

metadata.extraction_comment: Numerical large-order checks (relative-error equations and sequences confirmed only by Richardson extrapolation) carry rigor 'numerical'. Defined-term edges were added for every later use flagged by the finishing step, except where the word is used in another sense ('step' of a recursion, 'elementary' calculation, homogeneity 'weight').

nodes.statement: To be more specific, let us consider some observable Phi := langle cal O rangle and denote by Phi^(0)_k the k-loop coefficients of its perturbative expansion (in some adequate coupling constant).
nodes.raw_latex: To be more specific, let us consider some observable $\Phi := \langle {\cal O} \rangle$ and denote by $\Phi^{(0)}_{k}$ the $k$-loop coefficients of its perturbative expansion (in some adequate coupling constant).

nodes.statement: For simplicity, let us assume there are only two instanton actions, A_1 and A_2, and the nonperturbative sectors are organized as (n,m) corresponding to an exponential factor of the form sim n A_1 + m A_2. The reader immediately realizes that a door is now open towards new phenomena: indeed, if the two actions happen to be mathbb Z-linearly dependent, then there is n^star, m^star such that n^star A_1 + m^star A_2 = 0 and the nonperturbative exponential contributions ``collapse'' to order one, no longer suppressed or enhanced. Such phenomena have appeared recurrently in recent string theoretic examples . In these cases both the large-order resurgence relations as well as the transseries structure will change, in order to incorporate new (nonperturbative) resonant sectors, and logarithms may appear throughout. Because general physical problems may depend upon many parameters, it is conceivable that resonance is ``tunable'' and may generically appear in many examples. We shall later discuss in a very explicit example how this may come about and what are its implications.

Applying the Borel--Pad\'e (BP) resummation to the asymptotic series chi_(0rightarrow1) (k), we expect to obtain a resulting meaningful quantity which may be subtracted out of the original perturbative sequence F_k^(0,0)\, frac2pii A^kGamma(k). Looking back at , one writesfootnoteRecall that SF_(0rightarrow2) = S_1^2. F_k^(0,0)\, frac2pii A^kGamma(k) - SF_(0rightarrow1) times cal S_0 BP_N [chi_(0rightarrow1)] (k) &simeq& \\ && hspace-200pt simeq 2^-k\, SF_(0rightarrow2) left( F_0^(2,0) + fracF_1^(2,0) left( 2A right)k + fracF_1^(2,0) left( 2A right) + F_2^(2,0) left( 2A right)^2k^2 + cdots right) + O(3^-k), nonumber and the analysis would now proceed akin to what we did earlier. But, as we said, in many situations, including the case we are now addressing, the BP approximant to chi_(0rightarrow1) will indeed have poles along the positive real axis. We shall deal with them by simply performing a lateral resummation, cal S_0^- BP_N [chi_(0rightarrow1)] (k), which integrates right below the real line. This will then produce a result with both real and imaginary components. As it turns out, the real contribution will be similar to above, and can be compared to the exponential order 2^-k of the large-order behaviour of the perturbative series, just as in .

nodes.statement: For simplicity, let us begin by assuming that there is only one critical point to be crossed, which we shall label by~m. The location of this singularity is s = V (boldsymbolz^*_m) - V (boldsymbolz^*_n) = V^*_m - V^*_n equiv V^*_nm, which is nothing but the relative potential of the critical points n and m. In order for the integration in to be well defined, the integration contour needs to avoid this singularity. This can be done by avoiding it either from above or from below, by simply shifting to either theta^+ or theta^-. Each of these shifts will yield a different result for the partition function Z^(n) (hbar), which we shall denote by Z_pm^(n) (hbar), respectively. Their difference, Z_+^(n) (hbar) - Z_-^(n) (hbar), essentially yields the monodromy that cal B[Psi_n](s) acquires as one moves from theta^- to theta^+. This monodromy is induced by the monodromy of the vanishing cycle, cal V_n (s), as ones goes around the singularity V^*_nm in a counter-clockwise fashion, and which is captured by the Picard--Lefschetz formula cal V_n ( r_nm\, e^i left( phi + 2pi right) ) = cal V_n ( r_nm\, e^iphi ) + left(-1right)^fracd left(d-1right)2\, S_nm\, cal V_m ( r_nm\, e^iphi ).

nodes.statement: item Forward motions: forward resurgence motions which connect the original sector Phi_(3,2) with the sectors Phi_(3-ell_1,3), ell_1=0,1,2,3 (the alien-lattice vectors defining these motions are boldsymbolell=left(-ell_1,1right), i.e., the ``upwards'' motions of figure~); and iterations thereof (meaning we can still reach sectors Phi_(1,4) and Phi_(0,5) by iterating the boldsymbolell=left(-1,1right) motion, and indefinitely reach sectors Phi_(3,m) with m>3 by iterating the boldsymbolell=left(0,1right) motion). Or else, forward resurgence motions which connect the original sector Phi_(3,2) with the sectors Phi_(4,2-ell_2), ell_2=0,1,2 (the alien-lattice vectors defining these motions are boldsymbolell=left(1,-ell_2right), i.e., the ``rightwards'' motions of figure~); and iterations thereof (meaning we can still reach sector Phi_(5,0) by iterating the boldsymbolell=left(1,-1right) motion, and indefinitely reach sectors Phi_(n,2) with n>4 by iterating the boldsymbolell=left(1,0right) motion). The angle theta_boldsymbolell on the complex Borel plane, associated to each of the corresponding projected directions, is simply theta_boldsymbolell = arg left( boldsymbolell cdot boldsymbolA right).
nodes.raw_latex: \item \textit{Forward motions}: forward resurgence motions which connect the original sector $\Phi_{(3,2)}$ with the sectors $\Phi_{(3-\ell_{1},3)}$, $\ell_{1}=0,1,2,3$ (the alien-lattice vectors defining these motions are $\boldsymbol{\ell}=\left(-\ell_{1},1\right)$, \textit{i.e.}, the ``upwards'' motions of figure~\ref{fig:sec5-2d-lattice}); and iterations thereof (meaning we can still reach sectors $\Phi_{(1,4)}$ and $\Phi_{(0,5)}$ by iterating the $\boldsymbol{\ell}=\left(-1,1\right)$ motion, and indefinitely reach sectors $\Phi_{(3,m)}$ with $m>3$ by iterating the $\boldsymbol{\ell}=\left(0,1\right)$ motion). Or else, forward resurgence motions which connect the original sector $\Phi_{(3,2)}$ with the sectors $\Phi_{(4,2-\ell_{2})}$, $\ell_{2}=0,1,2$ (the alien-lattice vectors defining these motions are $\boldsymbol{\ell}=\left(1,-\ell_{2}\right)$, \textit{i.e.}, the ``rightwards'' motions of figure~\ref{fig:sec5-2d-lattice}); and iterations thereof (meaning we can still reach sector $\Phi_{(5,0)}$ by iterating the $\boldsymbol{\ell}=\left(1,-1\right)$ motion, and indefinitely reach sectors $\Phi_{(n,2)}$ with $n>4$ by iterating the $\boldsymbol{\ell}=\left(1,0\right)$ motion). The angle $\theta_{\boldsymbol{\ell}}$ on the complex Borel plane, associated to each of the corresponding projected directions, is simply $\theta_{\boldsymbol{\ell}} = \arg \left( \boldsymbol{\ell} \cdot \boldsymbol{A} \right)$.

0 &=& -\left( m-m^\prime \right) \delta_{k,2}\, \delta_{\boldsymbol{n},\boldsymbol{0}} + 3\, m\, m^\prime\, \delta_{k,3}\, \delta_{\boldsymbol{n},\boldsymbol{0}} + 4 \left( m\, m^\prime \left( \boldsymbol{n} \cdot \boldsymbol{A} \right)^2 - \left( m-m^\prime \right) \left( \boldsymbol{n} \cdot \boldsymbol{A} \right) -1 \right) c^{(\boldsymbol{n})}_k + \nonumber \\
&&
+ 4 \left( k-1 \right) \left( 2\, m\, m^\prime \left( \boldsymbol{n} \cdot \boldsymbol{A} \right) - \left( m-m^\prime \right) \right) c^{(\boldsymbol{n})}_{k-1} + m\, m^\prime \left( 3 + 4 \left(k-1\right) \left(k-2\right) \right) c^{(\boldsymbol{n})}_{k-2} - \nonumber \\

&&
+ 12\, m\, m^\prime\, \sum_{n_1^\prime=0}^{n_1}\, \sum_{n_2^\prime=0}^{n_2}\, \sum_{k^\prime=0}^{k} \left( \left( \boldsymbol{n}^\prime \cdot \boldsymbol{A} \right) c^{(\boldsymbol{n}^\prime)}_{k^\prime} + \left( k^\prime-1 \right) c^{(\boldsymbol{n}^\prime)}_{k^\prime-1} \right) c^{(\boldsymbol{n}-\boldsymbol{n}^\prime)}_{k-k^\prime} + \nonumber \\
&&
+ 4\, m\, m^\prime \left( \sum_{n_1^\prime=0}^{n_1}\, \sum_{n_1^{\prime\prime}=0}^{n_1^\prime}\, \sum_{n_2^\prime=0}^{n_2}\, \sum_{n_2^{\prime\prime}=0}^{n_2^\prime}\, \sum_{k^\prime=0}^k\, \sum_{k^{\prime\prime}=0}^{k^\prime}\, c^{(\boldsymbol{n}-\boldsymbol{n}^\prime)}_{k-k^\prime}\, c^{(\boldsymbol{n}^\prime-\boldsymbol{n}^{\prime\prime})}_{k^\prime-k^{\prime\prime}}\, c^{(\boldsymbol{n}^{\prime\prime})}_{k^{\prime\prime}} \right),
\label{eq:ell_nl_recursion}
\end{eqnarray}
